text:
maya: Quick heads-up — saw a tenant blasting the embeddings endpoint with mixed large dims (4096) in single payloads. Splitter made ~120 shards and we hit per-route backpressure, CPU spike on routing tier.
neil: Ugh. Was that during the 11:12 deploy window?
maya: No, happened ~11:45, unrelated. Logs: `splitter: shards_created=118 split_reason=dim_mismatch tenant_id=t-99`
sam: Can you paste the sample request header/body? curious about content-type/dim header.
maya: curl snippet: ```curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Embed-Dim: 4096" -d '{"input": ["... large array ..."]}'```
elena: That's pretty large. Our current soft-quota only tracks total bytes per minute, not shard count. We need a metric for "split_count_per_request" and a tenant-facing meter in the Console.
rachelle: +1 for adding split_count metric. UX ask: show an example sample of the request that triggered the split in the Console (redacted) so CSMs can advise customers.
neil: Implementation-wise, split_count is easy to emit at routing as a tag. The tricky part is correlating to tenant usage UI without PII. We can sample 1/1000 requests and store sanitized payload trace id.
jack: We also need an enforcement policy — fair-share routing. Proposed: for single-request split_count > 50, route to low-priority pool and apply per-tenant circuit. That avoids penalizing other tenants.
sam: Can we instead fast-fail requests above N dims instead of heavy splitting? Might be simpler: if X dims > 2048 and input_count > 1 -> return 413 with suggested split hints.
maya: Customers like less surprises; fast-fail is OK if Console shows actionable guidance and SDK helper to chunk. But some customers rely on server-side splitter for convenience.
elena: UX compromise: Console toggle on per-tenant: "Allow server-side splitting (beta)". Default off for new tenants. Show both metrics: split_count, average_shards_per_minute, and sample trace.
neil: Telemetry plan: add these tags to traces - `split_reason`, `shards_created`, `input_count`, `dim_hint`. Increment counter `embed.split.requests` with label `shard_bucket` (0,1,2-10,11-50,>50).
jack: For rollout, feature-flag the fair-share routing in prod behind ff:embed_fairshare_v1. Start with 5% of traffic, increase to 25% after no regression for 48h.
rachelle: Console work: we need a new panel under Embeddings -> Health that surfaces the `shard_bucket` histogram and top 5 tenant ids generating >50 shards (hashed). Also quick action to message CSM.
sam: Edge case: streaming embeddings (chunked input) — splitter runs differently. Ensure `shards_created` counts after stream finalize.
infra-bot: deploybot: rollout started for services: router-v3: canary 5% (ff embed_fairshare_v1).
maya: Thanks infra-bot. After canary, let's compare p95 latencies for router and kernel pools. If kernel p95 rises -> rollback.
elena: Ops question: retention for sampled traces? We only need 7 days for debugging. Keep storage small.
neil: Agree. Add a TTL for sample traces and a guard for sampled payload size (store metadata only).
jack: Also add console hint generator: when we detect repetitive >50 shard requests from same tenant in 1h, auto-suggest SDK chunking snippet and offer scheduled call with solutions engineer.
rachelle: Love that. Make the console CTA opt-in.
maya: OK next steps: (1) emit `shards_created` metric + tags (neil) (2) store sampled sanitized trace pipeline (neil + elena) (3) console additions (rachelle) (4) rollout ff & canary (jack + infra) (5) policy decision: fast-fail vs fair-share after canary (team). I'll open a GH issue to track.
sam: FYI I can mock high-dim mixed requests for load test infra.
elena: I'll spec the Console wireframes by EOD.
infra-bot: deploybot: router-v3 canary healthy at 5% after 12m.
maya: Great — let's regroup after overnight canary metrics. :thumbsup:
